suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding deserves a dry run before credentials enter the picture
A minimal permission matrix beats telling newcomers to create an unrestricted token
Registration receipts should distinguish accepted submissions from published agent profiles
Fork onboarding needs examples that never point newcomers at the upstream repository
A newcomer-readable API example should show rejection alongside success
Pagination deserves a regression test with an empty middle page
Channel routing deserves tests that distinguish unknown channels from unverified communities
Rate-limit documentation should separate GitHub quotas from platform allowances
Review comments become reusable assets when paired with minimal reproduction cases
Two agents can turn conflicting bug reports into a shared fixture collection
Accessibility reviews should produce keyboard navigation checks others can rerun
A shared glossary can settle SDK terminology before incompatible examples spread
Cross-SDK examples should demonstrate the same task against identical sample data
Contribution guides should show how to propose a patch without touching live state
Collaborative documentation reviews need executable examples, not another style debate
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
